build.details: Build succeeded. 0 Error(s), 1 Warning(s) (pre-existing CS0414 in ChildrenMisbehaviorManager.misbehaviorCheckInterval)

nonBlockingIssues.description: Pre-existing: openAiModelName field has no Scribe_Values.Look call in ApiSettings.ExposeData(). Missing before refactoring — not introduced by this feature.
chatLog field is declared 'private readonly' on mutable List<T>. readonly prevents reassignment but not mutation. Minor style concern.
Constructor does not explicitly call : base(game). Consistent with established project pattern (GameComponent base class lacks Game constructor). Not a bug.
TTSManager.Current?.GetVoices().Count potential null chain — practically safe since GetVoices() returns non-null list. Later commit (fix-existing-gamecomponents) added guards.
Pre-existing: unused field misbehaviorCheckInterval (CS0414 warning). Was present before conversion.

DateTracker_MapComponent.ExposeData() retains redundant DatingManager.Current.ExposeData() call causing double serialization. This was the only serialization path pre-conversion but is now redundant since GameComponent.ExposeData() is called automatically. Provides accidental backward compatibility for pre-conversion saves. Should be cleaned up eventually.
Pre-existing: IsConversationActive reads activeConversations.Contains() without queueLock while mutations are locked. Thread-safety concern from original code.
GameComponentTick() calls static methods which re-fetch Current from the game — minor inefficiency (double component lookup) but functionally correct.

suggestedGuidanceUpdates.suggestion: Update the 'Static Current accessors' convention to use fully-qualified 'Verse.Current.Game?.GetComponent<T>()' to disambiguate from the class's own 'Current' property. Current documentation says 'Current.Game?.GetComponent<T>()' which is ambiguous inside classes that define a 'Current' static property.
suggestedGuidanceUpdates.evidence: Features convert-tts-manager and all subsequent GameComponent conversions use 'Verse.Current.Game?.GetComponent<T>()' for disambiguation. All 6 converted GameComponents follow this pattern.

suggestedGuidanceUpdates.suggestion: Add convention: 'When converting a static class to GameComponent, remove any existing MapComponent.ExposeData() proxy calls that previously delegated to the static class. GameComponent.ExposeData() is called automatically by the engine. Leaving proxy calls causes double serialization.'
suggestedGuidanceUpdates.evidence: convert-dating-manager left DateTracker_MapComponent.ExposeData() calling DatingManager.Current.ExposeData() — a residual from when DatingManager was static and the MapComponent was the only serialization entry point. Now causes double write of 'dates' and 'dateCooldowns' keys.

suggestedGuidanceUpdates.suggestion: Document the nested settings access pattern: 'Settings fields are accessed via Settings.Api.X, Settings.Features.X, Settings.Prompts.X, Settings.Display.X, Settings.Gameplay.X. No direct field access on the top-level settings class.'
suggestedGuidanceUpdates.evidence: decompose-settings updated 51 consumer files to use the nested pattern. All future workers touching settings need to know this convention.

suggestedGuidanceUpdates.suggestion: Add Windows fallback note to refactor-worker skill's 'Initialize Environment' step: 'On Windows, .factory/init.sh may fail. Run the equivalent dotnet restore commands directly: dotnet restore SocialInteractions\SocialInteractions.csproj && dotnet restore SocialInteractions.Tests\SocialInteractions.Tests.csproj'
suggestedGuidanceUpdates.evidence: 5 out of 6 workers in this milestone reported init.sh failing on Windows with path resolution or dotnet-not-in-PATH errors. All successfully used direct dotnet restore as fallback. This is a systemic issue affecting every Windows worker session.

rejectedObservations.observation: Worker suggestion to add init.ps1 for Windows
rejectedObservations.reason: services.yaml already has explicit 'restore' command. The real issue is the skill referencing init.sh without documenting alternatives. Addressed in suggestedGuidanceUpdates for the skill.
